newsitem.title: POLAND: BRE jumps amid bank sector rebound.
newsitem.headline: BRE jumps amid bank sector rebound.

text.p: Polish Bank Rozwoju Eksport SA (BRE) jumped 9.9 percent to 78 zlotys in high turnover, reacting to recent losses along with much of the banking sector on Wednesday, traders said.
They said banks had probably bottomed out after falls averaging 30 percent in the last three months had made bank prices attractive and spurred demand.
Most banks rose or were flat on Wednesday, with large-cap BPH up 0.7 percent to 153.5 zlotys and Bank Slaski flat at 255 zlotys.
"The banks look really cheap so they finally rebounded. BRE's rebound is the strongest because its fall was the deepest," one trader said.
BRE fell about 40 percent since recording a 52-week high on February 13.
Banks had traded at an average 8.4 times historic earnings after Tuesday's session, with BRE's price-earnings ratio at 9.8.

Analysts said banks' weak first quarter earnings and little hopes for good earnings later this year signalled a limited upside and that the sector could soon stabilise after possibly gaining a few percent.
They said the late-May primary market offering of Poland's largest commercial bank, Bank Handlowy, was likely to additionally limit buying of listed banks.
